lessons.title: Personal hygiene in the packhouse
lessons.html:
Why hygiene matters

Fresh fruit is often eaten without cooking. If germs (bacteria and viruses) from dirty hands, toilets or dirty equipment get onto fruit, people who eat it can get very sick. Buyers and export markets check packhouses for hygiene. A packhouse that fails an audit can lose its customers, and workers can lose their jobs.

Hand washing

Your hands carry the most germs. Wash your hands with soap and clean running water:

  • Before starting work and after every break.
  • After using the toilet.
  • After eating, smoking, coughing, sneezing or blowing your nose.
  • After touching rubbish, rotten fruit, the floor or your face and hair.

How to wash hands properly

  1. Wet your hands with clean water.
  2. Use soap and rub palms, backs of hands, between fingers, thumbs and under nails for at least 20 seconds.
  3. Rinse well.
  4. Dry with a paper towel or hand dryer. Do not dry on your clothes.
  5. Use hand sanitiser if the packhouse requires it.

Clothing and appearance

  • Wear clean protective clothing (apron, overall, hairnet) every day. Do not wear it in the toilet or outside the work area if the rules say so.
  • Cover all hair with a hairnet; men may need a beard net.
  • Keep nails short and clean, with no nail polish or false nails.
  • Remove jewellery, watches and earrings, as the rules allow.
  • Cover cuts and sores with a waterproof plaster, usually blue so it can be seen if it falls off.

Health

If you have diarrhoea, vomiting, fever, or an infected wound, tell your supervisor before starting work. You may be moved to another job until you are well.

lessons.title: Keeping the workplace clean
lessons.html:
Rules in the work area

  • Never eat, drink, chew gum, smoke or spit in the packing area. Use the canteen.
  • Keep personal items such as phones, bags and food in the lockers.
  • Do not use glass in the packing area. Report any broken glass or hard plastic at once so the area can be cleared and fruit checked.
  • Keep fruit, cartons and packaging off the floor.

Cleaning and sanitising

Cleaning removes dirt, fruit pieces and juice. Sanitising kills germs that remain. Both are needed, in that order: you cannot sanitise a dirty surface.

Basic cleaning steps

  1. Remove fruit, waste and loose dirt.
  2. Wash with water and the approved detergent, scrubbing where needed.
  3. Rinse with clean water.
  4. Apply the approved sanitiser at the correct strength.
  5. Let it act for the time given, then rinse or leave to dry as the instructions say.

Using cleaning chemicals safely

  • Use only chemicals approved by the packhouse, at the dilution on the label or cleaning schedule.
  • Wear gloves, goggles and apron as required.
  • Never mix chemicals, for example bleach and acid cleaners, because they can give off poisonous gas.
  • Keep chemicals in labelled containers in the chemical store, never in food or drink bottles.
  • Do not spray chemicals near fruit or packaging.

Cleaning schedule

The packhouse has a cleaning schedule showing what to clean, how, how often and who does it. Sign the record when you finish. Clean colour-coded brushes and cloths are used for each area, for example toilets have their own colour that is never used on the line.

Pests and waste

Rats, mice, birds, flies and cockroaches carry germs. Keep doors closed, empty bins regularly, do not leave food lying around, and report any signs of pests. Do not move or touch bait stations.

Key points

  • Wash hands with soap after the toilet, breaks and touching dirty things.
  • Wear clean protective clothing, hairnets and blue plasters on cuts.
  • Report illness before starting work.
  • Clean first, then sanitise, using approved chemicals safely.
  • Never mix chemicals and keep pests out.
